name: link-storm
description: One initiator keeps window full link lifecycles in flight at once - establish a link, close it the instant it settles, refill the slot the moment the close settles - for the wall-time. Where establishment-churn pays one handshake at a time serially and concurrent-links holds N links open to measure table breadth, this churns establish/teardown AT breadth: it measures how fast a node can stand sessions up and tear them down when many are racing through the handshake together. No payload rides the link, so the establishment path is the whole cost - every cycle pays the full handshake crypto (the initiator's Ed25519 proof verify and X25519 session DH, the responder's proof sign and DH), table tracking, and teardown, the load a hub dialing or accepting a storm of short-lived links pays. window bounds the links open at once, so it stays under the link table's ceiling at any throughput.
conformance: established == closed at drain (every link that stood up was torn down) and failures == 0 for a Prns pair; the responder stays live across the whole storm. establish_per_sec is the throughput; a reactor that serializes the handshake crypto caps lower than one that fans the proof verify and session DH out to a worker pool.
